channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Overfitting the Validation Set Through Too Many Experiments
item.description: Run enough experiments against one validation set and you stop measuring generalisation, you start measuring luck. Here is why, with numbers.

item.title: Reproducibility: Seeds, Configs, and Runs You Can Rerun
item.description: Most 'irreproducible' ML results fail for boring reasons: unpinned seeds, missing configs, undocumented data splits. Here is how to fix that properly.

item.title: Data Augmentation That Helps vs Augmentation That Leaks
item.description: Augmentation only helps when it happens after splitting. Get the order wrong and your validation score becomes a lie.

item.title: Reading a Confusion Matrix Beyond Accuracy
item.description: Accuracy is a single number that can lie to you. A confusion matrix, read properly, tells you where and why your model actually fails.

item.title: BLEU and Its Limits for Evaluating Generated Text
item.description: BLEU counts matching word chunks, not meaning. Here is why that gap matters and how to evaluate generated text more honestly.

item.title: Perplexity: What It Rewards and What It Ignores
item.description: Perplexity tells you how well a model predicts held-out text, but it says nothing about coherence, factuality, or usefulness. Here is what it quietly rewards and ignores.

item.title: Tokenization Choices and Why They Change Your Results
item.description: Tokenization looks like plumbing, but it decides what your model can see. Get it wrong and no amount of tuning will fix it.

item.title: Transfer Learning: Freeze, Fine-Tune, or LoRA?
item.description: Freezing, full fine-tuning, and LoRA all solve transfer learning differently. Here is how to choose based on data size, compute, and risk of overfitting.

item.title: Gradient Clipping and Exploding Gradients in RNNs
item.description: A practical look at why RNN gradients explode over long sequences, and how norm-based clipping keeps training stable without hiding real bugs.

item.title: Learning Rate: The First Hyperparameter to Tune
item.description: Tune the learning rate before anything else: it decides whether your model converges, stalls, or blows up entirely.

item.title: Dropout as an Ensemble, Not a Magic Switch
item.description: Dropout works because it approximates ensembling thousands of thinned networks, not because randomness alone regularises. Here is the intuition, worked through with numbers.

item.title: Why Batch Normalization Helps, and When It Hurts
item.description: Batch norm speeds up training by taming shifting activations, but it leans on batch statistics that can betray you at small batch sizes or test time.

item.title: Attention, Intuitively: Queries, Keys, and Values
item.description: Attention is a soft lookup table: queries ask, keys answer, values deliver. Here is that idea made concrete with numbers.

item.title: Embeddings 101: What Cosine Similarity Actually Measures
item.description: Cosine similarity measures angle, not distance. Understanding that difference will save you from subtle bugs in retrieval and clustering systems.

item.title: Train, Validation, Test: Why Three Splits Not Two
item.description: Two splits let your decisions leak into your test score. A validation set is what keeps your final number honest.

item.title: The Trap of Optimizing the Wrong Metric
item.description: High accuracy can hide a useless model. Here is why the metric you optimize quietly decides what your system actually learns.

item.title: Feature Scaling: Which Models Care and Which Do Not
item.description: A practical guide to why distance and gradient based models demand scaled features while tree based models shrug them off entirely.

item.title: Class Weights vs Resampling for Imbalanced Data
item.description: Class weights and resampling both target imbalance, but they change different things. Here is how to pick the right one and evaluate it honestly.

item.title: Early Stopping vs Regularization: Do You Need Both
item.description: Early stopping and regularization both fight overfitting, but they work through different mechanisms. Understanding the difference tells you when you need one, the other, or both.

item.title: A tuned GRU beat LoRA-fine-tuned GPT-2, here's why
item.description: A 117M-parameter transformer lost to a small recurrent net on every metric. Not because transformers are bad, but because the baseline was done properly.
